note: Rewritten from Sjöstedt 1900, Monographie der Termiten Afrikas. Nachträge, original in Latin (species diagnosis) and German (detailed description). This entry contains only the imago alata (alate) and cites Sjöstedt's original publication in Ent. Tidskr. XIX (1898) (Termes niger Sjöst., p. 12) as the basis of the name; the soldier and worker are not described in this paper. The page header is damaged by OCR and the page numbers are not preserved, so no page is given in the locator; in the measurements values such as "Exp. alar. 73" are in millimetres. Plate III, fig. A (alate) is not translated. The page numbers are largely lost in the OCR; from the surviving running heads (8, 12) the entry is inferred to be on about p. 9, and the printed original should be checked before a final citation.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Original Latin description: the alate is black and shining, the femora and tarsi slightly paler; the head much longer than wide, concave in the middle, with a small circular area in the centre; between the ocelli there is a low rounded ridge; the labrum is small and slightly swollen, black like the frons; the compound eyes are broadly oval and the ocelli far from them; the antennae have 19 segments, brownish black with narrow white rings, segment 3 slightly longer than segments 2 and 4; the pronotum is as wide as the head (with compound eyes), semicircular, with a small concavity in the middle, its anterior margin raised and deeply incised in the middle, its posterior margin incurved; the wings are brownish smoky, the costa slightly darker, the media close to the subcosta, and in the forewing the media and submedia do not separate posteriorly. German description: the body is shining black, the tibiae, tarsi, mesothorax and metathorax tinged with brown; the head is slender, about a quarter longer than the width between the outer margins of the compound eyes, rather flat, with a shallow concavity in the middle, in the centre of which lies a small area bounded by a circle; between the ocelli there is a very distinct wall-like ridge; the labrum is the same colour as the black frons, not markedly swollen, with a shallow longitudinal groove in the middle; the compound eyes are large and slightly oval; the ocelli are round and large, their distance from the compound eye almost exceeding their own diameter, with a broad shallow pit in front of them; the labrum is blackish brown with a pale transverse line and a yellowish base; the antennae are blackish brown with narrow pale rings, with 19 segments, segment 2 slightly shorter than segment 3. Measurements: wing span 73 mm; length with wings 42 mm; wing length 34 mm; wing width 8.5 mm; body length (with head) about 20 mm.
